name: fix_ruby_yaml_unsafe_load
description: Fixes a Ruby config loader using YAML.unsafe_load (arbitrary object instantiation) to use safe_load
prompts: ConfigLoader.load in lib/config_loader.rb parses a YAML config string, but it uses YAML.unsafe_load, which instantiates arbitrary Ruby objects named by !ruby/object tags in the input - so an untrusted config can drive object construction (a remote-code-execution foothold). lib/app_config.rb calls this loader. Fix load() so it only accepts plain data (hashes, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans) and refuses !ruby/object payloads - use YAML.safe_load. Plain configs like "name: app" must still parse normally. Keep the method name and signature; you should not need to modify app_config.rb.

setup_files.lib/config_loader.rb:
require "yaml"

module App
  class ConfigLoader
    # Parse a YAML config string into plain data.
    # BUG: unsafe_load will instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects named by
    # !ruby/object tags in the input - an untrusted config can trigger
    # object construction (a remote-code-execution foothold). Only plain
    # data (hashes, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans) should be allowed.
    def self.load(text)
      YAML.unsafe_load(text)
    end
  end
end
setup_files.lib/app_config.rb:
require_relative "config_loader"

module App
  class AppConfig
    def self.from_yaml(text)
      data = ConfigLoader.load(text)
      { name: data["name"], port: data["port"] }
    end
  end
end

test_setup_files.test/config_loader_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "../lib/app_config"

# A stand-in for any class an attacker might name in a !ruby/object payload.
class Gadget
  attr_accessor :pwned
end

class ConfigLoaderSecurityTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_plain_config_loads
    cfg = App::AppConfig.from_yaml("name: app\nport: 8080\n")
    assert_equal({ name: "app", port: 8080 }, cfg)
  end

  def test_rejects_ruby_object_payload
    payload = "--- !ruby/object:Gadget\npwned: true\n"
    assert_raises(StandardError) { App::ConfigLoader.load(payload) }
  end
end

reference_solution.lib/config_loader.rb:
require "yaml"

module App
  class ConfigLoader
    # Parse a YAML config string into plain data only. safe_load refuses
    # !ruby/object tags, so an untrusted config cannot instantiate arbitrary
    # Ruby objects.
    def self.load(text)
      YAML.safe_load(text)
    end
  end
end

files.lib/config_loader.rb:
require "yaml"

module App
  class ConfigLoader
    def self.load(text)
      YAML.safe_load(text, permitted_classes: [Gadget, Symbol], aliases: true)
    end
  end
end
